guide_enrichment.narrative: Our modest lean toward Rutgers starts with the passing-game matchup. Our numbers rate Rutgers’ passing efficiency much more favorably than Maryland’s pass defense, and we also see Rutgers having a path to create scoring opportunities. Maryland’s early defensive results are notable, including 10 sacks through two games, but we are not treating that small sample as proof that the underlying matchup favors the defense.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Rutgers’ passing offense against Maryland’s pressure. Maryland’s early sack production can disrupt the area in which our numbers give Rutgers its clearest advantage. If Rutgers handles that pressure, we can see why the underdog stays competitive; if not, Maryland has a direct route to creating separation. We see enough matchup support for Rutgers to disagree slightly with the market, but not enough value at the available price to move beyond a pass.

recent_game.fact: Maryland improved to 2-0 with a 38-14 road win over UConn on Sept. 12, 2026.
Maryland produced 475 total yards and 27 first downs against UConn, including 350 passing yards and 125 rushing yards.
Maryland converted 8 of 15 third downs, possessed the ball for 35:31 and committed no turnovers against UConn.
Maryland's defense held UConn to 223 total yards, 12 first downs and 3-of-11 third-down conversions while recording five sacks.
Maryland had two scoring drives longer than 90 yards against UConn, its first game with multiple 90-yard drives since 2018.

opponent_notes.fact: In Maryland's 2025 game at Rutgers, quarterback Malik Washington rushed for 164 yards and one touchdown, including a 73-yard touchdown run, while passing for 98 yards and one touchdown.
Running back DeJuan Williams rushed 14 times for a then-career-high 64 yards at Rutgers in 2025.
Linebacker Daniel Wingate made 12 tackles with a half tackle for loss at Rutgers in 2025.
Defensive back Lavain Scruggs recorded 10 tackles and an interception at Rutgers in 2025.
Cornerback Jamare Glasker recorded four tackles and two tackles for loss at Rutgers in 2025.

quarterback.fact: Sophomore Malik Washington is Maryland's returning starting quarterback and started all 12 games as a true freshman in 2025.
Washington completed 53 of 72 passes for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions through Maryland's first two games of 2026.
Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns against UConn, including a program-record 18 consecutive completions.
Transfer quarterback Cardell Williams is the backup; he completed 4 of 5 passes for 60 yards and a touchdown and rushed five times for 49 yards against Hampton.

offensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's starting offensive line against UConn was left tackle Rahtrel Perry, left guard Amory Hills, center Michael Hershey, right guard Ryan Howerton and right tackle Isaiah Wright.
Amory Hills made his first Maryland start at left guard against UConn after transfer Tellek Lockette started the opener at that position.
Rahtrel Perry had made 39 career starts, including 14 at Maryland, and owned the team's longest active offensive starting streak.
Transfer wide receivers Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. combined for 18 catches, 236 yards and two touchdowns against UConn.
Gladding had 14 receptions for 187 yards and two touchdowns through two games, while Durr had 16 receptions for 147 yards and one touchdown.
Iverson Howard rushed 26 times for 121 yards and three touchdowns through two games.
USC transfer Harry Dalton III scored two rushing touchdowns at UConn and had scored in each of his first two games for Maryland.

Maryland added 17 offseason transfers, including wide receivers Gladding, Durr and Ejani Shakir; running backs Dalton and Terrez Worthy; tight end Preston Howard; offensive lineman Tellek Lockette; and quarterbacks Cardell Williams and Jack Capaldi.

defensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's listed defensive starters against UConn included Lavon Johnson, Eyan Thomas, Nashir Taylor, Sidney Stewart, Trey Reddick, Daniel Wingate, Jamare Glasker, Amari Jackson, Jordan Scruggs, Messiah Delhomme and Lavain Scruggs.
Sidney Stewart recorded six tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one sack and a forced fumble against UConn after leading Maryland with seven sacks as a freshman in 2025.
DD Holmes led Maryland with 2.5 sacks through two games, while Eyan Thomas and transfer Derrick LeBlanc each had two sacks.
Freshman linebacker Zion Elee recorded his first career sack and forced a fumble against UConn.
Maryland added defensive-line transfers Lavon Johnson from Texas, Derrick LeBlanc from UCF, and Armon Parker and Jayvon Parker from Washington.
Maryland returned 74 percent of its 2025 defensive production, including 2025 leading tackler Daniel Wingate and freshman All-American Sidney Stewart.

coaching_changes.fact: Clint Trickett took over as Maryland's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach for 2026 after serving as Jacksonville State's offensive coordinator in 2025.
Matt Barnes returned to Maryland as special teams coordinator after two seasons as Mississippi State's co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
Randy Starks became Maryland's defensive line coach, and Kyle Schmitt took over the tight ends room.
